assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstration of Sr clocks with fractional uncertainty near 1e-18, push frequency metrology two orders beyond the caesium standard. This is measurement science of the kind that opens new physics: tests of relativity and constancy of constants, relativistic geodesy, dark-matter searches and the route to a redefinition of the second. Originality of the magic-wavelength idea and its clean laser-spectroscopy realization are clear.
assessment.attribution: Katori is the originator of the lattice-clock concept, and Ye's group (with Hall's frequency-comb heritage at JILA) delivered the leading accuracy and stability. Two laureates is a clean configuration; Hall and Hänsch were already recognized in 2005, and Ludlow, Hinkley and others at NIST/JILA are not in the credited list. The relative weight of Katori versus Ye is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs (JILA, RIKEN, NIST, PTB, SYRTE) confirm 1e-18-level performance, and international comparisons and the SI-redefinition roadmap are progressing. Timing is ripe; the redefinition itself is not yet complete but is not required for prize-worthiness.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the Hall-Hansch 2005 prize as already covering the frequency-comb part so that clocks are a distinct, sufficiently novel step.
Exact division of credit with Peter Zoller-style theory and with ion-clock work (Wineland, Rosenband), which lies outside the credited names.
Details of the original magic-wavelength proposal history are recalled from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry turns matter-wave coherence into inertial, gravitational and rotational sensors, with measurements of g, G, the fine-structure constant and equivalence-principle tests. The concept is original, the technique is general, and it fits the principle that progress is limited by what can be measured and how accurately.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard demonstrated early atom interferometry with gratings, Bordé gave the Ramsey-Bordé interferometer theory and scheme, and Kasevich (with Chu) realized the laser-pulse gravimeter and gyroscope that define the field. Schmiedmayer (also credited) and Chu, who already won in 1997 for cooling, complicate the allocation. Three of four credited names are chosen; Kasevich's role is the most central for modern precision work.
assessment.maturity: Cold-atom gravimeters are commercial and field-tested, but the fundamental-physics headline results (equivalence principle at 1e-12 level, large-momentum-transfer beams) are still evolving and no single decisive discovery exists. Maturity is good for methodology, moderate for new-physics impact.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be seen as a technique or sensing award rather than a discovery.
Overlap with the 1997 and 2001 prizes and the exclusion of Schmiedmayer and Chu from this configuration.
Priority between Bordé's theory and the experimental first demonstrations of 1991 is recalled from memory and not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realized the Hubbard model with controllable parameters: the superfluid-Mott transition, fermionic Hubbard physics, quantum gas microscopes with single-site resolution. It created quantum simulation as an experimental tool and is conceptually and technically deep.
assessment.attribution: The Jaksch-Zoller-Cirac proposal and the Greiner-Hänsch-Bloch Mott experiment are decisive; Bloch led the field's growth, Greiner the single-site microscope and Mott-insulator experiment, Esslinger the Fermi-Hubbard realization. The credited list has five names, which exceeds three, so theory (Cirac, Zoller) is omitted here, an unavoidable and contestable choice.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many groups; quantum simulation is now mainstream. The scientific payoff on open condensed-matter problems (for example the Fermi-Hubbard pseudogap and d-wave regime) is still developing, so some may say it is early for a completed story.
uncertainties: Difficulty of capturing theory and experiment in three names; Zoller and Cirac are better placed under the trapped-ion or Rydberg entries.
Whether quantum simulation has delivered a genuinely new physics result beyond emulating known models.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single NV centres in diamond established a room-temperature solid-state qubit and nanoscale quantum sensor of magnetic fields, temperature and strain. It is a clear case of quantum measurement, spanning single-molecule spectroscopy ideas, spin readout and sensing in biology and materials.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's 1997 single-centre optical detection and Jelezko's coherent manipulation are decisive; Lukin, Hanson and others developed registers, entanglement and sensing applications. The credited trio is a coherent configuration, though Hanson, Awschalom and Wrachtrup overlap with B005.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated, applications in magnetometry, NMR and biology are growing; quantum networks are still developing. The discovery is mature enough.
uncertainties: Overlap and potential split with the optical spin-interface entry B005.
Whether sensing impact is yet broad enough versus the earlier 2012 and 2025 quantum-control prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realization of strongly interacting Fermi gases with tunable Feshbach resonances, the BEC-BCS crossover and the observation of vortices and universal thermodynamics brought a paradigmatic strongly correlated system into the laboratory. The physics is fundamental and original, linking superconductivity, neutron matter and unitary gases.
assessment.attribution: Grimm's molecular BEC and crossover work, Salomon's Fermi-gas studies and Thomas's early strongly interacting gas are all central; Deborah Jin and Ketterle, key contributors, are not in the credited list (Jin deceased, which complicates fairness). The configuration is a reasonable but not unambiguous one.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed and mature, now more than two decades old; recognition is arguably late rather than early, and Ketterle's 2001 prize covers a related area.
uncertainties: Missing credited figures such as Jin, which weakens the attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller trapped-ion quantum gate proposal and its experimental realization led to high-fidelity entangling gates, algorithms and quantum simulation with ions. It is a foundational pathway to quantum computing, originated in theory and then proven in the lab.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 proposal; Blatt's group demonstrated the gate, teleportation and large-scale entanglement. Wineland, already recognized in 2012, and Monroe/Wineland-NIST work are not credited, which complicates a clean division of credit.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and ongoing in commercial platforms; the 2012 prize on single-quantum-system control partly covers the area, so timing is a question.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 Wineland-Haroche prize and with 2025 circuit prize.
Whether theory and experiment should be paired with Monroe or Wineland's NIST work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brought strong light-matter coupling to superconducting artificial atoms and underpins most present superconducting quantum processors, dispersive readout and microwave quantum optics. It is a concrete realization of cavity-QED ideas on a chip and has been enormously influential.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf made the 2004 proposal and demonstration; Schoelkopf and Wallraff led the experiments, Blais the theory. Girvin is also credited and is difficult to leave out; four names exceed the limit.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and independently replicated, but the 2025 prize to Clarke, Devoret and Martinis for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits makes near-term recognition of a closely related field less likely.
uncertainties: Proximity to the most recent circuit-related prize.
Allocation among four credited names, with Girvin left out of this proposed set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Ti:sapphire laser and Kerr-lens and semiconductor-absorber mode locking made the practical femtosecond laser, enabling attosecond physics, frequency combs, precision spectroscopy and biomedical imaging. It is an enabling tool of great impact for atomic physics and optics.
assessment.attribution: Moulton introduced the Ti:sapphire gain medium, Sibbett and colleagues demonstrated Kerr-lens mode locking, and Keller invented SESAM mode locking. Credit among these is reasonably separable, though the Kerr-lens work involved several others (Spence, Kean, Sibbett) not credited.
assessment.maturity: Mature, universally used. The prizes in 1999, 2005, 2018 and 2023 already recognized adjacent areas, so the uniqueness of this recognition is a concern, but the laser invention itself remains unrecognized.
uncertainties: Overlap with prizes for femtochemistry, frequency combs, chirped pulse amplification and attosecond pulses.
Incomplete credited list for the Kerr-lens discovery.
